attributes.morphology: rod-like in transverse section, honeycomb-shaped, elongated in vertical direction

evidence.quote: The cellular structure presents a rod-like morphology that is honeycomb-shaped in the transverse section (Fig. 2b) but more elongated in the vertical direction (Fig. 2d). The grain A in a dendritic configuration stands out quite strikingly (Fig. 8d) with protrusion along different <001> directions. Similarly, grain B extends to an “L” shape by changing the growth direction along three orthogonal <001> directions.

attributes.morphology: fish-scale in YZ plane, horizontally elongated in XY plane

evidence.quote: Apart from the horizontally elongated features along the scanning direction in XY plane (Fig. 2a), melt tracks in YZ plane exhibit approximately fish-scale morphologies (Fig. 2c).

The combination of perturbations in the melt pool affecting the local solidification conditions and the thermal stresses due to the high temperature gradient causes the slight deflection of cell growth direction [17], leading to the formation of LAGBs dominantly parallel to the <001> directions (Fig. 3h).

attributes.location: low content at cell boundaries, relatively denser within cells

evidence.quote: Unlike the dense dislocation network that overlaps with cell boundaries in other LPBF superalloys [33,34], a very low content of dislocations at the cell boundaries but relatively denser dislocations within cells are found in the present study.

attributes.composition: C, Ti, Cr, Nb, Mo enriched

evidence.quote: Occasionally, a stacking fault (SF) connected with a pair of dislocations is present in Fig. 10f. At ~1344 ◦C, the solidification begins with the formation of primary γ phase cells.
Then the nucleation of nano-sized MC-type carbides from the inter-cellular liquid takes place near a temperature of 1313 ◦C.
The solidification terminates with a eutectic reaction L → γ + MC (~1277 ◦C).
After solidification, γ′ phases precipitate from the supersaturated γ matrix when cooling down below the γ′ solvus (~1158 ◦C).
